feature_network_reset-resetting-network-.title: Resetting network settings
feature_network_reset-resetting-network-.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Resetting network settings

If you are having trouble connecting to the Internet you may need to reset your network connections. Resetting your network connections will disconnect any Bluetooth devices connected to your device and disconnect your device from any Wi-Fi networks it is connected to.

steps.text: From the Settings screen, scroll to General management.

notes:
Note: 

Resetting your network settings will reset all your cellular and VPN settings. To reset Wi-Fi network settings, instead tap Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Settings.

feature_device_views_sim-inserting-and-r.title: Inserting and removing the nano SIM card
feature_device_views_sim-inserting-and-r.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Inserting and removing the nano SIM card

Learn how to insert, remove, and replace a SIM card in your device.

steps.text: Locate the combined nano SIM / microSD card tray on the side of your device.
notes:
Note: 

You must have a nano SIM card inserted in your phone to place calls, access the internet, download apps and share pictures over your carrier's network.

steps.text: Press the card insertion/removal tool into the combined nano SIM / microSD card tray pinhole and push in until the tray releases.
Slide the combined nano SIM / microSD card tray out of its slot.
notes:
Note: 

A nano SIM card may already be inserted in your phone.

steps.text: Insert or remove the nano SIM card into or from the tray with the gold contacts facing the front of the phone.
Press the combined nano SIM / microSD card tray back into its slot until it clicks, making sure it's secure.

feature_data_roaming-changing-roaming-se.title: Changing roaming settings for a trip
feature_data_roaming-changing-roaming-se.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Changing roaming settings for a trip

When traveling internationally, you may want to turn data roaming on and off to conserve data and minimize unwanted fees.

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Connections.
Tap or slide the Data Roaming switch to ON.
notes:
Note: 

Turning data roaming on allows you to connect to data services while roaming. Turn data roaming off to keep from incurring significant charges.

155860-can-t-send-or-receive-email.title: Can't send or receive email
155860-can-t-send-or-receive-email.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Can't send or receive email

Communication disruptions in electronic messaging stall important correspondence and lead to missed notifications. Checking transmission protocols and server configurations clears stuck queues, corrects sync errors, and ensures seamless message routing.

steps.text:
If you are unable to send and receive email messages, there are steps you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Check your mobile or Wi-Fi signal
Force Stop & Clear your App Cache
Restart your device
Check your email account settings
Force sync your Google Account
Remove and re-add email account
options: Next: Check your cellular or Wi-Fi signal

steps.text:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Turning off Airplane Mode re-enables your phone's Wi-Fi, cellular data, and Bluetooth radios to restore your device's connection to the internet, which may be a reason why you can't send or receive email.
Toggling it on and off also forces the phone to drop stale connection states and re-establish a fresh, clean link with local cell towers and network routers.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.text:
Check your connection
Check the cellular signal status icon in the upper-right corner of your device. Generally, the more bars that are displayed, the better the connection; if you have low or no signal, that may be the reason why you're experiencing connectivity issues.
If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. If no Wi-fi icon is shown, you may need to connect to a Wi-fi network. If your Wi-fi icon has an exclamation point, there is a problem with your connection.
options: Next: Force Stop & Clear your App Cache

steps.text:
Force Stop & Clear your App Cache
Clearing the app cache wipes corrupted temporary background files and broken sync indexes without deleting your email account or personal data.
Force-stopping the app fully shuts down any stuck or frozen background processes so your email app can initiate a clean reconnection to the servers when reopened.
Tap Force stop within Settings > Apps on your respective app, which is also where you'll find the option to clear the app's cache.
links: Clearing the cache and data for an individual app

steps.text:
Try restarting your device
Restarting your device clears frozen app processes, flushes temporary system memory, and forces a fresh connection to your cellular or Wi-Fi network.
links: Turning Your Phone On and Off
options: Next: Check your email account settings

steps.text:
Check your email account settings
Take a moment to make sure your login details and other options are correct, so your phone can properly send and receive messages.
These Account Settings are typically found in your Settings app > Accounts and Backup
options: Next: Remove and re-add your email account

steps.text:
Remove and re-add email account
Removing and re-adding your email account clears out broken security tokens, password mismatches, and corrupted server connection profiles on your phone.
It forces the phone to re-authenticate with the right email servers and download fresh, correct incoming and outgoing server settings from scratch.
You can remove and re-add your email account within the Accounts and Backup section of your Settings app, under Manage accounts.
links: Removing an account

155863-can-t-install-an-app.title: Can't install an app
155863-can-t-install-an-app.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Can't install an app

Software installation failures block new software deployment and keep critical tools from launching. Troubleshooting setup errors helps identify storage shortages, bypass permission restrictions, and resolve package corruption so applications run properly.

steps.text:
If you are unable to install an app, there are several steps you can take to try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Check your mobile or Wi-Fi signal
Check your available storage
Restart your device
options: Next: Check your cellular or Wi-Fi signal

steps.text:
Check your connection
Check the cellular signal status icon in the upper-right corner of your device. Generally, the more bars that are displayed, the better the connection; if you have low or no signal, connectivity issues may be the reason why you're having issues downloading an app.
If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. If no Wi-fi icon is shown, you may need to connect to a Wi-fi network. If your Wi-fi icon has an exclamation point, there is a problem with your connection.

Check your available storage
You'll want to confirm that your phone has enough space required beyond the app’s listed size, which you can typically do within Settings > Device Maintenance or Device Care.
If your free space drops below a safe threshold (typically 10–15%), your operating system may automatically block downloads to prevent system errors.
links: Managing your storage space on your phone

steps.text:
Try restarting your device
Restarting your phone clears frozen background download queues and flushes corrupted temporary system memory that causes downloads to stall on "Pending."
It also forces fresh network and account authentication connections with the app store servers so the download can start from a clean slate.
links: Turning Your Phone On and Off

155864-can-t-connect-to-wi-fi-or-interne.title: Can't connect to Wi-Fi or internet
155864-can-t-connect-to-wi-fi-or-interne.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Can't connect to Wi-Fi or internet

Loss of network connectivity disrupts online communication, daily operations, and remote access to essential tools. Diagnosing link failures helps restore online functionality, resolve router communication conflicts, and re-establish stable signal transmission.

steps.text:
If you are unable to connect to a Wi-Fi network or hotspot, or if you're encountering slowdowns on your existing connection, there are several actions you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Connect to Wi-Fi
Turn off Intelligent Wi-Fi
Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi
Restart your device
Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem
Reset your network settings
options: Next: Make sure airplane mode is off

steps.text:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Turning off Airplane Mode re-enables your phone's Wi-Fi, cellular data, and Bluetooth radios to restore your device's connection to the internet.
Toggling it on and off also forces the phone to drop stale connection states and re-establish a fresh, clean link with local cell towers and network routers.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.text:
Connect to Wi-Fi
Within the Settings app, take a moment to confirm that your phone is connected to a Wi-Fi network. A icon will indicate an active connection to whatever Wi-Fi network you've tapped on (or previously saved).
Note: If you're successfully connected to Wi-Fi, but you're getting a "No Internet Connection" message, there may be an issue with your Wi-Fi router/gateway that you'll need to troubleshoot.
links: Connecting to a Wi-Fi network

steps.text:
Turn off Intelligent Wi-Fi
Disabling Intelligent Wi-Fi stops your phone from constantly switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data in the background. It fixes connection drops and "Connected, no internet" bugs by forcing the phone to maintain a stable, continuous lock on your selected Wi-Fi network.
Typically, this setting is found under Settings > Connections > Wi-Fi, via the triple-dot menu in the upper-right corner.
Note: Older devices may call this feature "Adaptive Wi-Fi" or "Smart Network Switch."
options: Next: Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi

steps.text:
Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi
Forgetting and reconnecting to Wi-Fi wipes out saved network credentials, IP settings, and cached security handshake data for that specific router on your phone.
Typically, you'll be able to do this via the Settings app > Connections > Wi-Fi. From there, tap the Settings Cog next to you Wi-Fi network to access advanced network settings, and you'll be able to forget the Wi-Fi network. Reconnect, enter your password, and see if that fixes your issue.
links: Connecting to a Wi-Fi network

steps.text:
Try restarting your device
Restarting your phone clears stuck network drivers and flushes temporary system memory. This can clear temporary software glitches and forces your phone to establish a fresh, stable connection to the internet.
links: Turning Your Phone On and Off
options: Next: Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem

steps.text:
Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem
Restarting your Wi-Fi router or modem clears its temporary memory and fixes local IP address assignment conflicts. This gives your phone a fresh, clean network path to reconnect without affecting any saved settings on your phone.

Reset your network settings
Resetting your network settings clears out your phone's saved connection info and lets it start fresh, often fixing problems that Airplane Mode or a restart couldn't.
Before you reset, write down anything you'll need to re-enter, since this action erases:
Wi-Fi passwords
Bluetooth pairings
VPN settings
APN (Access Point Name) settings, if you entered these manually to connect to your carrier's cellular network
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.
links: Resetting network settings

155865-battery-draining-quickly.title: Battery draining quickly
155865-battery-draining-quickly.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Battery draining quickly

Excessive power depletion can severely impact device performance, daily usability, and long-term hardware health. Identifying the root causes of rapid power loss helps you resolve background process conflicts, optimize energy settings, and restore your device to normal operational capacity.

steps.text:
If your device battery is draining quickly, there are several actions you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Manage your battery
Manage your background apps
Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences

Manage your battery
Within the Settings app's Battery section, you can:
View which apps and system components are using the most battery life
View your overall battery usage statistics
Enable Battery Protection to extend your battery's life
Check your charging settings
Together, these features should help you get a better sense of how your battery is being used and whether you're charging your device optimally for long-term battery health.
links: Managing the battery

steps.text:
Manage your background apps
Managing your background apps prevents unused software from silently running, tracking location, or fetching data when you aren't using it.
Putting these apps to sleep stops unnecessary processor activity, directly reducing constant power drain on your device.
links: Managing app power usage and force closing apps
options: Next: Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences

steps.text:
Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences
Adjusting your auto-lock and brightness preferences reduces display power draw, which is the single largest consumer of battery life on a phone.
Shortening the screen timeout and dimming screen intensity ensures your display isn't draining energy when you aren't actively looking at it.
links: Adjusting the screen timeout and brightness

155885-wi-fi-calling-isn-t-working.title: Wi-Fi Calling isn't working
155885-wi-fi-calling-isn-t-working.intro:
Galaxy A15 5G
Wi-Fi Calling isn't working

When Wi-Fi calling is on, your device can make and receive calls via Wi-Fi networks. Your device will choose to make calls via Wi-Fi or over a cellular network based on which signal is stronger at the time.

steps.text:
If Wi-Fi Calling isn't working on your device, a few quick checks will tell you whether the problem is temporary or something that needs a fix.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Check that Wi-Fi Calling is turned on
Confirm you're connected to a working Wi-Fi network
Use Airplane Mode to "soft-reset" your connection
Update your emergency address
Restart your device
Check for carrier or software updates
Reset network settings
Find additional support to address your problem
options: Next: Check Wi-Fi Calling is turned on

steps.text:
Check Wi-Fi Calling is turned on
First, let's confirm that Wi-Fi Calling is turned on. You can find this setting in a couple of places, depending on your phone.
To check:
Open the Phone app and tap the three-dot menu (More options) in the top corner.
Tap Settings, then tap Wi-Fi Calling.
Check that the toggle is turned on. If it's off, tap it to enable it.
If you don't see this option there, try:
Settings app > Connections (or Network and Internet) > Wi-Fi Calling
Note: Wi-Fi Calling availability depends on your plan and device. If you don't see the option in either place, your plan may not support it on your phone.
links: Activating Wi-Fi calling
options: Next: Confirm you're connected to Wi-Fi

steps.text:
Confirm you're connected to Wi-Fi
Wi-Fi Calling requires an active Wi-Fi connection. Check the Wi-Fi icon in your status bar and make sure you're connected to a working network, not just cellular data.
links: Connecting to a Wi-Fi network
options: Next: Check if Airplane Mode is enabled

steps.text:
Toggle Airplane Mode on and off
Turn Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then turn it off. This resets your device's network connections, including Wi-Fi and cellular radios.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.text:
Update your emergency address
Wi-Fi Calling uses this address to route emergency services if you dial 911, so it's important for it to be current.
Go to Phone app > More options (⋮) > Settings > Wi-Fi Calling, then tap Emergency Address to review or update it.

Restart your device
Power your device off completely, wait 10 seconds, then turn it back on. This clears temporary network glitches that can block Wi-Fi Calling from connecting.
links: Turning Your Phone On and Off

steps.text:
Check for carrier or software updates
Go to Settings > Software Update to install any pending updates, and check with your carrier that Wi-Fi Calling is active on your line.
links: Checking for and installing system updates
options: Next: Reseat your SIM card (if applicable)

steps.text:
Remove and reinsert your SIM card
Note: This step only applies to devices with a physical SIM card. If your device uses an eSIM instead, skip to the next step.
Power off your device, remove the SIM card, wait a few seconds, then reinsert it firmly. This can resolve issues where your carrier isn't properly recognizing your account.
links: Inserting and removing the nano SIM card

steps.text:
Reset your network settings
Resetting your network settings clears out your phone's saved connection info and lets it start fresh, often fixing problems that Airplane Mode or a restart couldn't.
Before you reset, write down anything you'll need to re-enter, since this action erases:
Wi-Fi passwords
Bluetooth pairings
VPN settings
APN (Access Point Name) settings, if you entered these manually to connect to your carrier's cellular network
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.
links: Resetting network settings

steps.text:
Get additional support
If you're still having issues with Wi-Fi Calling on your device, you should contact your carrier for additional support. They'll be able to help identify if there's an issue on their end that's affecting Wi-Fi Calling (e.g. a problem with your account, your SIM, or your Wi-Fi Calling eligibility).

155886-mobile-hotspot-isn-t-working.intro:

Mobile Hotspot isn't working

Learn how to fix a personal hotspot that won’t connect. Follow this step-by-step user manual to troubleshoot connection drops, password issues, and cellular data errors.

steps.text:
Mobile Hotspot allows you to broadcast a Wi-Fi network from your phone based on your cellular connection.
If you're having issues setting up or using Mobile Hotspot, there are a few ways you can troubleshoot the issue.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure mobile hotspot is properly set up
Restart your phone
Check for updates
Check your cellular connection
Reset your network settings

Setting up Mobile Hotspot
Take a moment to check that Mobile Hotspot is enabled on your device. You'll also want to confirm that your carrier and service plan supports Wi-Fi hotspots, or else the feature may not appear (or you may not be able to enable it).
When setting up your Mobile Hotspot:
Go to Settings > Connections > Mobile Hotspot and Tethering > Mobile Hotspot and turn on the switch.
Make sure Mobile Data is enabled via Settings > Connections > Mobile Networks (or Data usage) > Mobile Data.
If devices are having trouble connecting, tap Configure under Mobile Hotspot and set the Band to 2.4 GHz. (You may need to turn your other devices' Wi-Fi off and back on before they'll successfully connect to your hotspot.)
You can also try forgetting the Wi-Fi network on your connecting device and reconnecting to your Mobile Hotspot, in case you accidentally saved an incorrect password or are encountering some other kind of connection issue.
links: Setting up mobile hotspot

steps.text:
Try restarting your phone
Restarting your phone is a quick, low-risk first step that can resolve many Mobile Hotspot issues. To restart your phone, try one of these two methods.
1) Physical buttons
Press and hold the Power button until the Power menu appears, then tap Restart.
On some models, hold the Power button and a Volume button together.
If nothing happens, try Power + Volume Up. If that doesn't work, try Power + Volume Down.
2) Quick Settings
Swipe down from the top of the screen, tap the Power icon, then select Restart.
If neither of these work, continue to the next step to force restart your phone.
links: Turning Your Phone On and Off

steps.text:
Check for updates
Next, you'll want to make sure your phone is running the latest version of Android, just in case that's somehow preventing you from using the Mobile Hotspot feature.
links: Checking for and installing system updates

steps.text:
Checking your cellular connection
It's possible that devices can connect to your Mobile Hotspot, but you have a weak or problematic cellular connection that's affecting your devices' performance.
Try turning off your Mobile Hotspot temporarily and use your phone as you normally would. Make sure you're not connected to a Wi-Fi network and try placing a call or loading a webpage.
If you're encountering issues, try switching your phone to Airplane Mode, waiting 15 seconds, and turning it off. Otherwise, try moving to a location with a stronger or more consistent cellular signal and testing Mobile Hotspot again to see if the issue is with your phone's connection or the hotspot.

Reset your network settings
Resetting your network settings clears out your phone's saved connection info and lets it start fresh, often fixing problems that Airplane Mode or a restart couldn't.
Before you reset, write down anything you'll need to re-enter, since this action erases:
Wi-Fi passwords
Bluetooth pairings
VPN settings
APN (Access Point Name) settings, if you entered these manually to connect to your carrier's cellular network
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.

steps.text:
Turn Bluetooth off and on
Under Connections in Settings you will find your Bluetooth settings. Tap into your Bluetooth settings and you can use the toggle to turn your Bluetooth on and off. This forces a complete reset of your Bluetooth settings.
options: Next: Pair with a different bluetooth device

steps.text:
Pair with a different bluetooth device
Pairing your phone with another bluetooth device can help you further diagnose and isolate the core issue.
If the secondary device connects fine. Your phone’s Bluetooth hardware and software are working. The issue is specific to the original device (e.g., its battery is low, it’s not in true pairing mode, or it needs a firmware update).

Within your bluetooth settings you will be able to access your device's settings that you want to unpair. Forgetting a Bluetooth device wipes out the outdated or broken passkey your phone saved, allowing both devices to reattempt a working connection from scratch.
